root_cause.text: The `aio_cmd` structure containing a `struct kiocb` with the `ki_write_stream` field was allocated using `kmalloc_flex` which does not zero-initialize memory, leaving the field uninitialized and potentially containing a bogus value that triggers an unintended write failure when compared against `max_write_streams`.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states "doesn't initialize the aio_cmd->iocb for the ki_write_stream... we may get a bogus ki_write_stream value, causing unintended write failure status when checking iocb->ki_write_stream > max_write_streams". The patch changes `kmalloc_flex` to `kzalloc_flex`, which ensures zero-initialization of the allocated memory, thereby setting `ki_write_stream` to zero.
